# [CS078] Database Access in Transport Layer (go.architecture.sql-in-transport-layer)

A package named handler, api, transport, web, http or controller calls methods of *sql.DB or *sql.Tx directly.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | LOW |
| **Category** | Architecture |
| **CWE** | - |
| **OWASP** | - |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

When handlers run queries themselves, request parsing, authorization and storage logic mix in one place: every handler must repeat the same scoping and error handling, and the queries cannot be tested without HTTP. A repository or store package behind an interface keeps the transport layer thin and gives queries one place to be reviewed.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
func (h *Handler) GetOrder(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	row := h.db.QueryRowContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE id = $1", r.PathValue("id"))
	_ = row
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
func (h *Handler) GetOrder(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	order, err := h.orders.Get(r.Context(), r.PathValue("id"))
	_, _ = order, err
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [go.architecture.sql-in-transport-layer]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    go.architecture.sql-in-transport-layer: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore go.architecture.sql-in-transport-layer -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** go.architecture.sql-in-transport-layer
```
